content_blocks.title: Worked example: Serving Downloads
content_blocks.expected_output: The helper rejects empty names and extensions outside the example allowlist, and request bodies are capped at 2 MiB. This is only one validation layer, not full content inspection.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Test harmless synthetic names and sizes. Store using a unique server-generated identifier, keep private files outside public static paths, and authorize downloads.

content_blocks.title: Before using this beyond practice
content_blocks.text: Validate untrusted input at the server boundary, keep secrets out of source code, and test the failure path. Optional extensions or hosting infrastructure are separate dependencies unless stated otherwise.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a fragment without checking its imports, app configuration or dependencies.
common_mistakes.why: Many Flask examples assume a configured app and a specific runtime or extension version.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the run instructions, record the Flask/Python version and test the smallest behavior first.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the successful request path.
common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, unsupported methods, unauthorized objects and service failures often have different behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a negative or boundary test and assert the status code and response contract.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a local example as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Secret management, concurrency, deployment, monitoring and failure recovery need separate design decisions.
common_mistakes.fix: Review the matching deployment and security references before publication or real use.
